themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints in CD 302 spiked to 3 complaints THIS WEEK versus a historical average of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a new or newly intensified source of disturbance affecting outdoor community spaces.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extremely rare statistical event
CD 302 includes major parks (Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn Bridge Park waterfront) where residents congregate
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department and identify specific park(s) affected; determine if event-related (concert, festival, construction) or chronic source
Canvass park users and nearby residents about timing, type of noise, impact on quality of life

themes_detail.label: Street Lights Failing
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 21 THIS WEEK from a 9.0 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 133% spike (z-score: 5.24)—indicating possible widespread outages or maintenance backlog in public lighting infrastructure.
evidence: 21 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.0 weekly average (133% increase)
Z-score of 5.24 indicates highly anomalous pattern
Annual CB budget requests for 'transportation infrastructure' suggest ongoing lighting concerns
reporting_angles: Request Con Edison and DOT data on outages, service calls, and repair timelines in CD 302 this week
Document specific blocks/intersections with darkened lights; assess public safety implications for nighttime pedestrians and cyclists

themes_detail.label: Construction Dust & Air Quality
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints surged to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO (433% above 1.1 weekly average, z-score: 3.84) while air quality complaints hit 8 TWO WEEKS AGO (146% above baseline, z-score: 3.66), suggesting active construction projects may be releasing hazardous particulates.
evidence: 6 construction lead dust complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 3.84)
8 air quality complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.2 weekly baseline (146% spike, z-score: 3.66)
1,198 DOB permit filings in past 90 days, including 854 alteration permits—heavy construction activity ongoing
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits filed in past 3 weeks with 311 complaint locations to identify problem project(s); verify lead compliance inspections
Interview residents near high-complaint areas about health symptoms (respiratory, children's blood lead levels); contact NYC Health Dept on lead testing

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints doubled to 32 LAST WEEK from a 16.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 97% spike (z-score: 5.2)—pointing to a sudden breakdown in street or facility cleanliness.
evidence: 32 unsanitary condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 16.2 weekly average (97% spike, z-score: 5.2)
Dirty Condition complaints also consistently high (278 total over 90 days), part of baseline problem
Spike coincides with period of high construction activity (1,198 DOB filings in past 90 days)
reporting_angles: Request DSNY (Sanitation) data on collection schedules, staffing absences, or service disruptions in CD 302 last week
Visit complaint hotspots to document conditions; determine if construction debris, waste accumulation, or vermin are the issue

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees & Urban Forest Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints climbed to 7 LAST WEEK from a 1.4 weekly baseline—a 409% increase (z-score: 6.56)—suggesting either a disease event, pest infestation, or deferred Parks maintenance affecting the neighborhood's tree canopy.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% spike, z-score: 6.56)
Spike is recent and localized; may signal disease (e.g., spotted lanternfly, emerald ash borer) or weather event
Annual CB budget requests for Parks equipment suggest maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks arborist unit for data on disease/pest reports, tree removals, and trimming activity in CD 302 in past 2 weeks
Identify the specific tree species and locations; consult arborist on cause and canopy recovery outlook
